questions.stem: Why were many passengers stranded at the railway station?
options: A) Because too many passengers headed home.
B) Because there was a terrible train accident.
C) Because a rare snowfall delayed trains.
D) Because all trains were delayed.

explain.定位:
More than 55,000 passengers were left stranded at this station in the south of the country after
a rare snowfall delayed trains.
在一场罕见的降雪导致列车延误后，这个位于该国南部的车站有超过 55,000 名旅客滞留。
explain.信号:
after 引出真正起因。答案句里 after a rare snowfall delayed trains 的 after 是因果信号
——它前面是结果（旅客滞留），后面才交代真正原因（罕见降雪致列车延误）。这与第一
步预读说的盯 after/because 完全吻合，听到 after 就该锁定这句。
explain.替换:
a rare snowfall delayed trains ↔ a rare snowfall delayed trains
原因短语整段对应
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
录音确实念到大量旅客返乡 millions of people are heading back to families，A 便把这
点改写成 too many passengers headed home 当原因。但这是春运的背景，旅客真正被
困是因降雪延误，A 用听得到的原词把背景偷换成起因，答非所问。
借用原文：millions of people are heading back to families
B) 未提及
a terrible train accident 把原因说成列车事故，但录音通篇只说 adverse weather
delayed trains（恶劣天气致延误），从未出现事故、相撞、伤亡等字眼。这是凭常识脑补
的无中生有，原文无据。
D) 偷换概念
录音说的是 adverse weather delayed trains，只讲天气延误了列车，并没说所有列车都延
误。all trains were delayed 偷偷加上 all 把范围放大到全部，与原文不符；况且它只复述
了延误这个结果，没回答 why。
借用原文：adverse weather delayed trains

questions.stem: When is this year's Chinese New Year according to the news report?

explain.定位:
Most of those trips will fall around next Monday's Lunar New Year.
这些出行大多将集中在下周一的农历新年前后。
explain.信号:
Lunar New Year 锁定所问事件。录音末句把时间 next Monday 直接挂在 Lunar New
Year 上，而题问的正是 Chinese New Year（即农历新年）。听到事件词 Lunar New Year
与时间词同句出现，就锁定这句，别被前面的别的时间干扰。
explain.替换:
next Monday's Lunar New Year ↔ Next Monday
时间词直接对应
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
录音确有 two weeks ago，但它说的是 40 天春运期 the 40-day period which started
two weeks ago 开始的时间，不是春节的时间。A 把这个听得到的时间挪来答春节，配错
了事件。
借用原文：the 40-day period which started two weeks ago
B) 原词陷阱
录音里 40 出现在 the 40-day period（为期40天的春运周期），B 却改写成 40 days later
（40天后）当春节时间。它盗用了听得到的数字 40，却既改了含义又配错了事件。
借用原文：the 40-day period
C) 原词陷阱
After the snowfall 借用了录音里的 snowfall 一词，把春节说成在降雪之后。但录音从没说
春节在降雪之后发生，降雪只是导致列车延误，与春节的日期没有时间关系，属硬凑的关
联。
借用原文：a rare snowfall delayed trains

questions.stem: Which country experienced the biggest decline in happiness according to the survey?

explain.定位:
Greece had the largest drop in the survey.
在这次调查中，希腊的降幅最大。
explain.信号:
最高级 largest 即答案信号。题干问 biggest decline，录音里对应的极性信号就是 Greece
had the largest drop in the survey 中的 largest drop——「最大降幅」这个最高级直接
标记了答案句。听到 the largest/the most 这类最高级，就要立刻锁定它修饰的对象。
explain.替换:
Greece had the largest drop ↔ Greek.
国名同指（Greece≈Greek）
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
录音开头 The United States has experienced a decline in happiness 确实念到美国「下
降」，The United States. 就靠这句勾人；但美国是「has experienced a decline」一般性
下降，问的是 biggest decline——降幅最大的是希腊不是美国，听到 decline + 美国就选
是典型的原词陷阱。
借用原文：The United States has experienced a decline in happiness
C) 原词陷阱
Iceland. 出现在录音念的「最幸福国家」名单 also included Switzerland, Iceland,
Norway 里，是被一并念到的原词；但它是「最幸福」名单成员，跟「下降最大」毫无关
系，纯属听到名字就想选的干扰。
借用原文：also included Switzerland, Iceland, Norway
D) 原词陷阱
Netherlands. 同样在 Canada, Netherlands, New Zealand 这串「最幸福国家」名单里被
念到，方向恰好相反——它是「最幸福」而非「下降最大」，是把幸福榜成员错安到「下
降」问题上的陷阱。
借用原文：Canada, Netherlands, New Zealand

questions.stem: What is this news report mainly about?
options: A) The decline of happiness in the U.S.
B) The optimistic future of Asians and Africans.
C) The life satisfaction in different countries
D) The driving factors to happiness.

explain.定位:
The United States has experienced a decline in happiness during the past ten years although it
remains among the world's happiest countries. The World Happiness Report found that ... The
happiest country in the world was Denmark ... Greece had the largest drop in the survey. ... a
top conclusion was that richer countries were happier than poor countries.
过去十年里美国的幸福感有所下降，尽管它仍位列世界上最幸福的国家之一。《世界幸福报
告》发现……世界上最幸福的国家是丹麦……在这次调查中希腊的降幅最大……一个主要结论
是富裕国家比贫穷国家更幸福。
explain.信号:
全篇围绕「各国幸福/满意度」。主旨题不靠单句，而靠全篇反复出现的话题：从 among
the world's happiest countries 到 The happiest country in the world was Denmark、
Greece had the largest drop、再到 richer countries were happier than poor
countries，整篇都在比较「不同国家」的幸福/生活满意度——这就是覆盖全篇的主线。
explain.替换:
richer countries were happier than poor countries ↔ The life satisfaction in different countries
举例→概括（详述归纳为主题）
a life satisfaction poll ↔ The life satisfaction in different countries
同词锚定主题（life satisfaction）
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
The decline of happiness in the U.S. 直接搬用开篇 The United States has experienced
a decline in happiness，原词高度重合极易误选；但它只覆盖第一句关于美国的局部信
息，后文丹麦、希腊、富国穷国等大半内容它都罩不住，是以偏概全。
借用原文：The United States has experienced a decline in happiness
B) 原词陷阱
The optimistic future of Asians and Africans. 取自录音中段 Asians and Africans are
the most optimistic people about their futures，原词都对得上；但这只是文中一笔带过
的枝节信息，范围窄到只剩两个人群，撑不起整篇主题。
借用原文：Asians and Africans are the most optimistic people about their futures
D) 原词陷阱
The driving factors to happiness. 对应结尾 Money was a big factor driving happiness
那段「驱动幸福的因素」，原词 factor/driving 都念到了；但「幸福的驱动因素」只是篇末
一小段，全篇主体是各国幸福/满意度的横向比较，不是谈成因，故偏题。
借用原文：Money was a big factor driving happiness

questions.stem: What is the research mainly about?
options: A) The types of gases released into the air.
C) The causes of breaking-off of the glaciers.
D) Climate impact on the temperature.

explain.定位:
Scientists found sea levels are rising faster today than any time over the past 3,000 years.
科学家发现，如今海平面上升的速度比过去 3000 年里任何时候都快。
explain.信号:
开篇首句点题、定全文主线。新闻常把核心信息放在第一句，这里开篇即 Scientists found
sea levels are rising faster today than any time over the past 3,000 years.，海平面上
升是后文升温、冰川、排放层层展开的源头主题，故首句即答案句。
explain.替换:
sea levels are rising faster today than any time over the past 3,000 years ↔
The fast-rising sea level.
整句概括成一个名词短语
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
录音确有 gases released into the air，The types of gases released into the air. 就盗这
串原词，但原文只是顺带解释升温成因，且谈的是「气体导致升温」不是「气体的种类」，
既以偏概全又答非所问。
借用原文：gases released into the air
C) 原词陷阱
The causes of breaking-off of the glaciers. 借了录音 break off from glaciers 的原词，
但这只是解释「为何升温会让海平面涨」链条里的一环，不是报道主旨，属把局部当全局。
借用原文：break off from glaciers
D) 原词陷阱
Climate impact on the temperature. 借了录音反复出现的 temperature，但原文逻辑是
「温度上升导致海平面上升」，温度是原因侧的铺垫，报道落脚仍在海平面；把铺垫说成主
旨，本末倒置。
借用原文：When temperatures rise, so do sea levels.

questions.stem: Who is the paper's lead author?
options: A) Stefan Rahmstorf from the Climate Impact Research Center.
B) Stefan Rahmstorf from the Potsdam Institute.
C) Robert Kopp from National Academy of Sciences.
D) Robert Kopp from Rutgers University.

explain.定位:
Robert Kopp, from Rutgers University in New Jersey, is the paper's lead author.
来自新泽西州罗格斯大学的 Robert Kopp，是这篇论文的第一作者。
explain.信号:
身份词 lead author 与题干完全对应。题干问 lead author，录音里 is the paper's lead
author 这个身份词原样出现，它前面紧贴的人名与机构就是答案；靠这个身份词锁句，比
逐字扫描快且准。
explain.替换:
Robert Kopp, from Rutgers University in New Jersey, is the paper's lead author ↔
Robert Kopp from Rutgers University.
人名机构原样对应、仅省略地点
explain.排除:
A) 张冠李戴
Stefan Rahmstorf from the Climate Impact Research Center. 用的是录音另一人 Stefan
Rahmstorf，但他是 the study's co-author（合著者），不是题干问的 lead author，把另
一人的身份安到本题答案上，且机构名也被改动。
借用原文：He is a professor of ocean physics at the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research
in Germany and the study's co-author.
B) 张冠李戴
Stefan Rahmstorf from the Potsdam Institute. 人名是合著者 Stefan、机构 Potsdam
Institute 也确属他，但他是 co-author 不是 lead author，仍是把另一人当第一作者，答非
所问。
借用原文：the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research in Germany
C) 偷换概念
Robert Kopp from National Academy of Sciences. 人名 Robert Kopp 是对的，但机构
被换成录音里另处出现的 National Academy of Sciences——那是发布研究的机构，不是
Kopp 所在的 Rutgers University，人对机构错。
借用原文：released Monday by the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

questions.stem: Since when have the temperatures around the Earth risen over a half-degree Celsius?

explain.定位:
The best estimates show that temperatures around the Earth have risen more than a half-
degree Celsius since 1880.
最佳估算显示，自 1880 年以来，全球气温已上升超过半摄氏度。
explain.信号:
题干 half-degree 原词回扣、紧跟其年份即答案。题干里的 half-degree Celsius 在录音
risen more than a half-degree Celsius since 1880 原样出现，紧跟它的 since 1880 就是
问的起始年份；靠这个独特短语锁句，能把它和录音里别处的 3000 年、两个 decade 等年
份分开。
explain.替换:
risen more than a half-degree Celsius since 1880 ↔ Since 1880.
起始年份原词对应
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
Since two decades ago. 借录音 The rise over the last two decades has been even
faster. 里的 two decades，但那讲的是「近二十年海平面涨得更快」，不是升温半度的起
点，配错了事件。
借用原文：The rise over the last two decades has been even faster.
B) 原词陷阱
Since 20th century. 蹭录音 the 20th century rise was "extraordinary" 里的 20th
century，但那是说「20 世纪的上升很惊人」，并非升温半度始于 20 世纪；原文给升温半
度配的明确是 1880。
借用原文：He said the 20th century rise was "extraordinary"
D) 原词陷阱
Since 2800 years ago. 由录音 gathered information going back 28 centuries（28 个
世纪≈2800 年）改来，但那是研究数据「追溯」的时间跨度，不是升温半度的起点，把研
究回溯年限错配成升温起始年。
借用原文：The sea level researchers gathered information going back 28 centuries.

questions.stem: Why are landfills unpopular according to the man?
options: A) They pollute the soil used to cover them.
B) They are harmful to nearby neighborhoods.
C) The rubbish in them takes long to dissolve.
D) The gas they emit is extremely poisonous.

explain.定位:
Landfills are places to dump waste, but they are unpopular because they can pollute the soil
used to cover them and that's bad for people who may build new homes there.
填埋场是倾倒垃圾的地方，但它们不受欢迎，因为它们会污染用来覆盖它们的土壤，这对日
后可能在那里盖新房的人来说是坏事。
explain.信号:
unpopular because…直接给出原因。答案句里 they are unpopular because they can
pollute the soil used to cover them 用 because 直接挂出「不受欢迎」的原因，正是题
干 unpopular 的应答点；听到 unpopular 紧跟 because，就该锁定其后那半句。
explain.替换:
they can pollute the soil used to cover them ↔ They pollute the soil used to cover them.
几乎原句搬运，仅去掉 can
explain.排除:
B) 原词陷阱
选项 They are harmful to nearby neighborhoods. 听着像录音里 that's bad for people
who may build new homes there，但原文说的是「对日后在那盖新房的人不好」，并非
「危害周边社区」，把「未来住户」偷换成「邻近社区」，答非所问。
借用原文：that's bad for people who may build new homes there
C) 未提及
选项 The rubbish in them takes long to dissolve. 说垃圾降解慢，但本段只讲了污染土
壤，从头到尾没提分解快慢，属凭常识臆造、录音未提及。
D) 未提及
选项 The gas they emit is extremely poisonous. 讲填埋场排剧毒气体，录音谈 landfills
时只字未提 gas，这是另一种常见环保常识被塞进来当干扰，属未提及。

questions.stem: What does the man say has contributed to the increase in amounts of waste over the years?

explain.定位:
10 or 20 years ago, you could buy milk in returnable, refillable glass bottles and many
people recycled voluntarily. Now you buy milk and other products in plastic bottles or
paper containers.
10 到 20 年前，你能买到用可退还、可重复灌装的玻璃瓶装的牛奶，很多人自愿回收。如今
你买的牛奶和其他产品都装在塑料瓶或纸盒里。
explain.信号:
过去 vs 现在的对比＝变化落点。答案句用 10 or 20 years ago 与 Now 拉出今昔对比：过
去是可回收玻璃瓶，现在变成塑料瓶、纸盒——这种「从前如何、如今如何」的对照，正是
垃圾增多的成因所在，对比转折处就是答案落点。
explain.替换:
plastic bottles or paper containers ↔ Packaging materials.
具体物→上位概念概括
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
选项 Growing population. 把垃圾增多归于人口增长，这是个貌似合理的常识推断，但录
音谈的是容器从玻璃瓶变塑料瓶，全程没提人口，属未提及。
C) 原词陷阱
选项 Changed eating habits. 听着呼应录音里反复的 buy milk，但原文变的是牛奶的「包
装」而非「吃喝习惯」，把容器变化偷换成饮食习惯变化，答非所问。
借用原文：Now you buy milk and other products in plastic bottles or paper containers
D) 原词陷阱
选项 Lower production cost. 蹭了录音里 the high cost of disposing of these things 的
cost，但原文说的是「处理成本高」，方向恰恰相反，且谈的是处置成本而非生产成本，既
偷换概念又与原文相反。
借用原文：Because of the high cost of disposing of these things in landfills

questions.stem: According to the man, how does recycling help the environment?
options: D) By making the most of materials.

explain.定位:
Recycling helps the environment mainly by saving energy. For example it takes 95% less
energy to produce recycled aluminum than to produce new aluminum.
回收帮助环境，主要是靠节省能源。比如，生产再生铝比生产新铝要少用 95% 的能源。
explain.信号:
mainly by 直接点明主要方式。答案句 Recycling helps the environment mainly by
saving energy 用 mainly by 直接挂出「主要靠……」的方式，正面回应题干 how；听到
mainly by，其后的内容就是答案，后半句的铝只是举例佐证。
explain.替换:
mainly by saving energy ↔ By saving energy.
去掉 mainly，措辞基本一致
explain.排除:
B) 原词陷阱
选项 By using less aluminum. 蹭了录音例句里反复出现的 recycled aluminum，但铝只
是用来「举例说明省能源」的，回收帮环境的主要方式是省能源，不是少用铝；把例证里的
名词当成主答案，答非所问。
借用原文：it takes 95% less energy to produce recycled aluminum than to produce new aluminum
C) 未提及
选项 By reducing poisonous wastes. 讲靠减少有毒废物护环境，但本段只说省能源，未提
任何 poisonous wastes，属脑补的环保常识、未提及。
D) 未提及
选项 By making the most of materials. 说靠充分利用材料，听上去与回收沾边，但录音这
段只讲省能源，没提「物尽其用」，属未提及。

questions.stem: Why does the man say everybody should make an effort to recycle?
options: A) We are running out of natural resources soon.
B) Only combined efforts can make a difference.
C) The waste problem will eventually hurt all of us.
D) All of us can actually benefit from recycling.

explain.定位:
If not you then who? If we combine our efforts, we can make a difference. Each of us
contributes to the waste problem.
如果不是你，那是谁呢？如果我们齐心协力，就能带来改变。我们每个人都给垃圾问题添了
一份。
explain.信号:
If we combine…we can＝表态收束句。答案句 If we combine our efforts, we can
make a difference 是被问者面对「一个人有用吗」的反问后给出的正面主张，用 if…then
句式收束全篇，正是题干要的理由；听到这种「合力才能改变」的强调收尾，就该锁定。
explain.替换:
If we combine our efforts, we can make a difference ↔
Only combined efforts can make a difference.
条件句改写成 Only 限定句，意思同一
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
选项 We are running out of natural resources soon. 把理由说成资源即将枯竭，这是常
见的环保论调，但被问者此处强调的是「合力」，没提资源耗尽，属未提及。
C) 原词陷阱
选项 The waste problem will eventually hurt all of us. 蹭了录音里的 Each of us
contributes to the waste problem，但原文说的是「我们每个人都在制造垃圾问题」，不
是「垃圾问题会伤害所有人」，把「人人有份制造」偷换成「人人受害」，答非所问。
借用原文：Each of us contributes to the waste problem
D) 偷换概念
选项 All of us can actually benefit from recycling. 把理由说成「人人都能从回收获
益」，蹭的是整段回收有好处的语境，但被问者强调的是「要合力」而非「都能受益」，理
由对象被偷换，答非所问。

questions.stem: Where is the woman planning to go?

explain.定位:
Could you please give me information on airfares from Miami to Bellingham, Washington?
请问能给我一些从迈阿密到华盛顿州贝灵厄姆的机票票价信息吗？
explain.信号:
from…to… 的方向结构。女士开口第一句 from Miami to Bellingham 用 from…to… 把
出发地和目的地一并交代：from 后是起点迈阿密，to 后才是终点贝灵厄姆。方向介词 to
就是锁定答案的信号。
explain.替换:
to Bellingham, Washington ↔ Bellingham.
原词直取目的地
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
Miami. 确实在录音里念到，但它在 from Miami 的 from 之后，是出发地。听到熟词就选
正中陷阱，方向词 from 已说明它不是要去的地方。
借用原文：from Miami
B) 原词陷阱
Vancouver. 在录音里出现于 why don't you book a flight to Vancouver Canada?，那是
男士为省钱提出的中转方案，不是女士本来要去的地方，且女士还回了 that's farther than
we want to go 表示不想去那么远。
借用原文：book a flight to Vancouver Canada
D) 未提及 Boston. 全程未在录音里出现，是凭空设置的干扰项，与本对话无关。

questions.stem: What is the woman's purpose in calling the man?
options: A) To get information on one-way tickets to Canada.
B) To inquire about the price of "Super Saver" seats.
C) To get advice on how to fly as cheaply as possible.
D) To inquire about the shortest route to drive home.

explain.定位:
We'd like advice on how to fly as cheaply as possible.
我们想要一些关于怎样尽可能便宜地坐飞机的建议。
explain.信号:
开门见山的诉求句。女士在第一段说完询价后紧接着点明诉求 We'd like advice on how to
fly as cheaply as possible，这是她主动说出的来电目的，目的题的答案信号就是这种『我
想要……』的直陈句。
explain.替换:
We'd like advice on how to fly as cheaply as possible ↔
To get advice on how to fly as cheaply as possible.
We'd like = To get advice
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
To get information on one-way tickets to Canada. 拼凑了录音后面才出现的 one-way
（one-way economy class fare）和 Canada（Vancouver Canada）。但 one-way 是男
士分析票价时的用词、Canada 是省钱绕道方案，都不是女士打电话的初衷。
借用原文：one-way economy class fare
B) 原词陷阱
To inquire about the price of "Super Saver" seats. 里的 Super Saver 来自男士的话
reserve the "Super Saver" seats，是他给的省钱细节，不是女士打电话来咨询的目的；而
且女士并未专门去问这种座位的价格。
借用原文：reserve the "Super Saver" seats
D) 原词陷阱
To inquire about the shortest route to drive home. 把结尾 if we don't decide to drive
的 drive 拿来用，但女士来电是问『怎么飞最便宜』，不是问开车最短路线；开车只是她最
后透露的后备方案。
借用原文：if we don't decide to drive

questions.stem: What does the man advise the woman to do?
options: C) Avoid trips in public holidays.
D) Book tickets as early as possible.

explain.定位:
Of course I'd recommend early booking, you ought to try to reserve the "Super Saver" seats.
当然，我建议尽早订票，你应该设法预订那种「超级优惠」座位。
explain.信号:
I'd recommend 建议信号词。男士说 I'd recommend early booking，recommend 是
明确的建议信号词，它后面的 early booking（尽早订票）正是他给的核心忠告；ought to
进一步加重了这条建议。
explain.替换:
I'd recommend early booking ↔ Book tickets as early as possible.
early booking = Book…as early as possible
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
Join a tourist group. 在录音里毫无依据，男士谈的全是订票时机、票种、绕道省钱，从未
提及加入旅行团。
B) 未提及
Choose a major airline. 同样无据。男士提的是经济舱、Super Saver 座位、提前订票，并
未建议挑选某家大航空公司。
C) 偷换概念
Avoid trips in public holidays. 看似贴合省钱话题，但男士说的是 If you can fly on a
Tuesday or Wednesday（建议挑周二周三飞），谈的是『错开高峰日』，并没有提到
public holidays（公共假日）这个词。选项偷换成了『避开节假日』。
借用原文：If you can fly on a Tuesday or Wednesday

questions.stem: What is the woman's Plan B for transport?

explain.定位:
I may call you back if we don't decide to drive.
如果我们没决定开车的话，我可能会再打电话给你。
explain.信号:
if we don't… 的条件假设。女士结尾说 I may call you back if we don't decide to
drive，if we don't decide to drive 这个条件句反过来透露：她们另有一个『开车』的备选
——若不开车才回头订机票。条件句就是 Plan B 的答案信号。
explain.替换:
if we don't decide to drive ↔ By car.
drive = by car
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
By coach. 对应录音 you can take a bus from Vancouver back to Bellingham 的 bus
（coach 即长途客车）。但那是男士设想『若飞温哥华，再坐车回贝灵厄姆』的回程衔接，
属于飞机方案的一部分，不是女士不坐飞机时的后备方案。
借用原文：take a bus from Vancouver back to Bellingham
C) 未提及
By bike. 在录音里没有任何依据，全程谈的是飞机、客车、开车，从未出现自行车。
D) 未提及
By train. 同样无据，男士提的接驳是 take a bus（坐客车），并非火车，火车这种方式录音
里根本没说。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about William Shakespeare?
options: A) There are mysterious stories behind his works.
B) There are many misunderstandings about him.
C) His works have no match worldwide.
D) His personal history is little known.

explain.定位:
Yet how many know Shakespeare, the person, the man behind the works? After centuries of
research, scholars are still trying to discover Shakespeare's personal history.
然而又有多少人了解莎士比亚这个人、了解作品背后的那个人呢？经过数百年的研究，学者
们至今仍在试图弄清莎士比亚的个人生平。
explain.信号:
转折词 Yet 后的反问 + still 强调。Yet how many know Shakespeare, the person 用 Yet
转折，把话锋从「作品人尽皆知」转到「这个人却没人了解」，紧接 scholars are still
trying to discover Shakespeare's personal history 用 still 强调至今没弄清——转折之后
才是说话者真正想说的那层意思。
explain.替换:
scholars are still trying to discover Shakespeare's personal history ↔
His personal history is little known.
「至今还在努力弄清」= 「鲜为人知」
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
录音确实多次说到 All kinds of myths surround the lives of well-known people，A 借
这些「谜 / 传说」造出 There are mysterious stories behind his works.，但录音说的是
「生平之谜」，不是「作品背后有神秘故事」——把谜安到了作品上，答非所问。
借用原文：All kinds of myths surround the lives of well-known people
B) 原词陷阱
录音说 Many myths arose about Shakespeare，B 据此说 There are many
misunderstandings about him.。误传确实有，但它只是文中一个枝节、且后文紧接着反
问「这些传说是真的吗？大概不是」，说话者的总意是「其人不为人知」，不是「误解很
多」，以偏概全。
借用原文：Many myths arose about Shakespeare
C) 过度推断
录音只说他是 one of the greatest English writers of the 16th and 17th centuries（那
个时代最伟大的英语作家之一），C 却升级成 His works have no match worldwide.（全
世界无人能比）。「之一」「英语作家」被偷改成「无双」「全世界」，程度和范围都被夸
大了。
借用原文：one of the greatest English writers of the 16th and 17th centuries

questions.stem: What do we learn about Shakespeare's father?
options: A) He moved to Stratford-on-Avon in his childhood.
B) He failed to go beyond grammar school.
C) He was a member of the town council.
D) He once worked in a well-known acting company.

explain.定位:
Shakespeare's father was a respected man in Stratford-upon-Avon, a member of the
town council.
莎士比亚的父亲是斯特拉福镇上一位受人尊敬的人，是镇议会的一名成员。
explain.信号:
题干主语 father 在原文直接出现。Shakespeare's father was a respected man in
Stratford-upon-Avon, a member of the town council 句首就是 Shakespeare's father，
与题干主语对上，是讲父亲的直接陈述句，答案信息（身份）就在这句尾部。
explain.替换:
a member of the town council ↔ He was a member of the town council.
原文身份几乎原样落在选项上
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
录音的 Stratford-upon-Avon 是说父亲所在地，A 却说 He moved to Stratford-on-Avon
in his childhood.——把地名搬来，又凭空加上「童年搬来」这个录音没说的时间，既张冠
李戴又无中生有。
借用原文：Shakespeare's father was a respected man in Stratford-upon-Avon
B) 张冠李戴
录音的 He sent young William to grammar school 讲的是父亲送儿子上文法学校，B 却
说 He failed to go beyond grammar school.，一是把「上学的儿子」当成了父亲，二是
录音说的是 William 没继续往上读，不是「没读完」，张冠李戴又混淆了对象。
借用原文：He sent young William to grammar school
D) 原词陷阱
He once worked in a well-known acting company. 里的「剧团」呼应了录音前文 An
acting company, for example, could change a play if they wanted to，但那是讲「当时
剧团能随意改剧本」，根本没说父亲在剧团工作，属把不相干的原词拿来安在父亲身上。
借用原文：An acting company, for example, could change a play if they wanted to

questions.stem: Why does the speaker say parts of Shakespeare's life will remain a mystery?
options: A) Writers of his time had no means to protect their works.
B) Possible sources of clues about him were lost in a fire.
C) His works were adapted beyond recognition.
D) People of his time had little interest in him.

explain.定位:
Some parts of Shakespeare's life will always remain unknown. The Great London Fire of
1666 burned many important documents that could've been a source of clues.
莎士比亚生平的某些部分将永远不为人知。1666 年的伦敦大火烧毁了许多本可成为线索来
源的重要文献。
explain.信号:
紧跟「仍是谜」之后给出的具体起因。录音先说 Some parts of Shakespeare's life will
always remain unknown，正对应题干「remain a mystery」，紧接着的 The Great
London Fire of 1666 burned many important documents that could've been a
source of clues 就是对「为什么」的直接交代——一场具体的火灾烧掉了本可做线索的
文献。
explain.替换:
The Great London Fire of 1666 burned many important documents ↔
Possible sources of clues about him were lost in a fire.
「火烧了文献」= 「线索来源毁于火」
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
录音确有 Authors of the time could not protect their works，A 据此写 Writers of his
time had no means to protect their works.。这句原文是用来解释「生平难从其作品中找
到」，并非回答「为什么部分生平永远成谜」——那个答案是后文的火灾，A 张冠李戴接错
了因果。
借用原文：Authors of the time could not protect their works
C) 过度推断
His works were adapted beyond recognition. 的「作品被改得面目全非」靠 An acting
company, for example, could change a play if they wanted to 里的 change a play 拼
凑，但原文只说剧团「可以改动剧本」，从没说改到 beyond recognition（面目全非），
是把程度夸大、无中生有。
借用原文：An acting company, for example, could change a play if they wanted to
D) 未提及
People of his time had little interest in him. 听起来也像个原因，但录音通篇没说同时代
的人对他缺乏兴趣，这是凭常识臆造的解释，属未提及。

questions.stem: Why does the speaker say "a headache is important"?
options: A) It shows you have been ignoring your health.
B) It can seriously affect your thinking process.
C) It is an early warning of some illness.
D) It is a symptom of too much pressure.

explain.定位:
A headache is important because it can be the first warning of a serious condition that could
probably be controlled if discovered early.
头痛之所以重要，是因为它可能是某种严重病症的最初预警，而这种病症若能及早发现，或
许就能得到控制。
explain.信号:
because 引出理由。答案信号是因果连词 because：题干问 Why，原文恰好用 A
headache is important because it can be the first warning of a serious condition 给
出理由，because 后面那半句就是答案所在。
explain.替换:
the first warning of a serious condition ↔ an early warning of some illness
同义改写：first→early、condition→illness
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
It shows you have been ignoring your health. 说头痛表明你一直忽视健康，原文谈的是
头痛预警疾病、以及不该用止痛药掩盖，从未说头痛源于"忽视健康"，属凭常识推演出的内
容。
B) 原词陷阱
It can seriously affect your thinking process. 借了原文 serious 的"严重"色彩，却把头痛
的重要性偷换成"严重影响思维"；原文只说头痛是 serious condition 的预警，从没说它影
响 thinking process。
借用原文：the first warning of a serious condition
D) 答非所问
It is a symptom of too much pressure. 把头痛说成"压力过大的症状"，原文虽提到头痛与
紧张（tension headaches），但解释"头痛为何重要"时给的理由是"疾病预警"，并未说它
是压力的症状，答非所问。
借用原文：rubbing and pressing the neck muscles

questions.stem: What does the specialist suggest we do with headaches?

explain.定位:
A headache specialist once said, "Masking symptoms is not the best way of treatment.
Sometimes it is wiser to stand still than to advance in darkness."
一位头痛专家曾说："掩盖症状并不是最好的治疗方法。有时候，原地不动比在黑暗中前行
更明智。"
explain.信号:
专家引语＋否定评价。答案信号是专家被直接引述的话加上否定评价：Masking symptoms
is not the best way of treatment，specialist said 锁定说话人，not the best way 是"不
该这么做"的劝告，反过来即"应避免掩盖症状"。
explain.替换:
Masking symptoms is not the best way of treatment ↔ Avoid masking symptoms
否定句转成 Avoid 的同义
explain.排除:
A) 答非所问
Reduce our workload. 减少工作量，原文只在讲头痛危害时提到 employee with a
headache does less work，从未把"减少工作量"作为专家的处理建议，属答非所问。
借用原文：The employee with a headache does less work.
B) 原词陷阱
Control our temper. 借了原文 In a flash of temper 的 temper 一词，但原文那句是描述
头痛者发脾气的危害，不是专家让我们"控制脾气"的建议，听到 temper 就选会中招。
借用原文：In a flash of temper, he or she may upset his fellow workers
C) 与原文相反
Use painkillers for relief. 用止痛药缓解，恰恰是原文批评的做法——If a person removes
the warning, day after day, with a painkiller, he or she may pass the point of easy
control，专家的态度是反对而非建议，方向相反。
借用原文：he or she may pass the point of easy control

questions.stem: What does the speaker say helps relieve the symptoms of common headaches?
options: A) Lying down and having some sleep.
B) Rubbing and pressing one's back.
C) Going out for a walk.

explain.定位:
Rest, quiet and fresh airs stop many common headaches. Lying down and possibly falling
asleep may help.
休息、安静和新鲜空气能止住许多普通头痛。躺下来、甚至睡上一觉，可能会有帮助。
explain.信号:
stop／help 引出缓解办法。答案信号是 stop many common headaches 和 may help 这
两个"奏效"的标志词：Rest, quiet and fresh airs stop many common headaches. Lying
down and possibly falling asleep may help，紧跟其后列出的就是缓解普通头痛的办法。
explain.替换:
Lying down and possibly falling asleep may help ↔ Lying down and having some sleep
几乎同义：falling asleep＝having some sleep
explain.排除:
B) 偷换概念
Rubbing and pressing one's back. 揉按的是 back（背），但原文说的是 rubbing and
pressing the neck muscles——揉按的是脖子（neck）；动作原词照搬、部位被换，是典
型细节偷换。
借用原文：rubbing and pressing the neck muscles
C) 过度推断
Going out for a walk. 外出散步，原文只提到 fresh airs（新鲜空气）有助缓解，并没有说
要"出去散步"这个动作，属由 fresh air 过度联想出来的未提及内容。
借用原文：Rest, quiet and fresh airs stop many common headaches.
D) 未提及
Listening to light music. 听轻音乐，原文列举的缓解办法是休息、安静、新鲜空气、躺下
入睡、揉按脖子、热敷、规律进食，从头到尾没提"听音乐"，属未提及。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say is the biggest budget mistake?
options: B) Having no budget plans at all.
D) Leaving no room for large bills.

explain.定位:
The biggest budget mistake is no budget at all.
最大的预算错误就是根本没有预算。
explain.信号:
最高级 the biggest 直接亮判定。录音里 The biggest budget mistake is no budget at
all. 用最高级 the biggest 把结论直接说出，这种最高级判定句就是答案信号，听到 the
biggest 就该锁这一句。
explain.替换:
no budget at all ↔ Having no budget plans at all.
几乎原义改写
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
Depending heavily on loans. 谈靠贷款度日，听着像理财困境，但原文 The biggest
budget mistake is no budget at all. 说的最大错误是没预算，全篇没说靠贷款，属答非所
问的联想干扰。
C) 答非所问
Spending beyond one's means. 入不敷出确实是种财务问题，开头 money traps 也让人
联想，但题目问的是 the biggest mistake，原文明确锁定没预算，C 不是被点名的那个最
大错误。
D) 原词陷阱
Leaving no room for large bills. 说没给大额账单留余地，原文 we just put all the bills
in a pile 确实提到 bills，但那是举例说明没预算的样子，并非把没给大账单留余地定为最大
错误，盗 bills 一词来误导。
借用原文：we just put all the bills in a pile

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about the so-called fixed expenses?
options: A) Many of them can be cut.
B) All of them have to be covered.
C) Their payment cannot be delayed.
D) They eat up most of the family income.

explain.定位:
Look for expenses that can be cut back, and don't give up in the face of high fixed expenses.
Many of these can be reduced too.
找出那些可以削减的开支，碰到高额的固定支出也别放弃，其中很多也是可以削减的。
explain.信号:
出现对象词 fixed expenses 后紧跟判定。录音点到对象词 high fixed expenses 后，紧接
着 Many of these can be reduced too. 给出判定——这些大多也能削减；对象词后面紧
跟的那句定性就是答案句。
explain.替换:
Many of these can be reduced too ↔ Many of them can be cut.
reduce=cut 近义替换
explain.排除:
B) 与原文相反
All of them have to be covered. 说全都必须照付，正好和原文 Many of these can be
reduced too. 说很多能削减唱反调，且 All 把话说满，是反向加极端的干扰。
借用原文：Many of these can be reduced too
C) 未提及
Their payment cannot be delayed. 讲付款不能拖延，原文谈固定支出只说能不能削减，
从没提付款时间能不能拖，属原文未涉及的内容。
D) 原词陷阱
They eat up most of the family income. 说固定支出吃掉大半家庭收入，原文确实提到
income，但谈的是房租占 more than 25% of your income，并未说固定支出整体吞掉大
部分收入，借 income 一词制造像是的错觉。
借用原文：more than 25% of your income

questions.stem: What does the speaker suggest people do to save housing expenses?
options: A) Rent a house instead of buying one.
B) Discuss the problem in the family.
D) Move to a cheaper place.

explain.定位:
If housing takes more than 25% of your income, for example, consider moving to a cheaper
place or renting out an extra room.
举例来说，如果住房花掉了你收入的四分之一以上，可以考虑搬到便宜点的地方，或者把多
余的房间租出去。
explain.信号:
条件句 If...consider 引出建议。录音 If housing takes more than 25% of your income,
for example, consider moving to a cheaper place，用 If...consider 这种条件加建议的句
式给出办法，consider 后面接的动作就是答案信号。
explain.替换:
moving to a cheaper place ↔ Move to a cheaper place.
近乎原句保留
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱

A) Fast-food firms have to be a thick-skinned bunch. Health experts regularly criticise them severely for selling food that makes people fat. Critics even complain that McDonald's, whose logo symbolises calorie excess, should not have been allowed to sponsor the World Cup. These are things fast-food firms have learnt to cope with. But not perhaps for much longer. The burger business faces more pressure from regulators at a time when it is already adapting strategies in response to shifts in the global economy.

B) Fast food was once thought to be recession-proof. When consumers need to cut spending, the logic goes, cheap meals like Big Macs and Whoppers become even more attractive. Such "trading down" proved true for much of the latest recession, when fast-food companies picked up customers who could no longer afford to eat at casual restaurants. Traffic was boosted in America, the home of fast food, with discounts and promotions, such as $1 menus and cheap combination meals.

C) As a result, fast-food chains have weathered the recession better than their more expensive competitors. In 2009 sales at full-service restaurants in America fell by more than 6%, but total sales remained about the same at fast-food chains. In some markets, such as Japan, France and Britain, total spending on fast food increased. Same-store sales in America at McDonald's, the world's largest fast-food company, did not decline throughout the downturn. Panera Bread, an American fast-food chain known for its fresh ingredients, performed well, too, because it offers higher-quality food at lower prices than restaurants.

D) But not all fast-food companies have been as fortunate. Many, such as Burger King, have seen sales fall. In a severe recession, while some people trade down to fast food, many others eat at home more frequently to save money. David Palmer, an analyst at UBS, a bank, says smaller fast-food chains in America, such as Jack in the Box and Carl's Jr., have been hit particularly hard in this downturn because they are competing with the global giant McDonald, which increased spending on advertising by more than 7% last year as others cut back.

E) Some fast-food companies also sacrificed their own profits by trying to give customers better value. During the recession companies set prices low, hoping that once they had tempted customers through the door they would be persuaded to order more expensive items. But in many cases that strategy did not work. Last year Burger franchisees(特许经营人) sued(起诉) the company over its double-cheeseburger promotion, claiming it was unfair for them to be required to sell these for $1 when they cost $1.10 to make. In May a judge ruled in favour of Burger King. Nevertheless, the company may still be cursing its decision to promote cheap choices over more expensive ones because items on its "value menu" now account for around 20% of all sales, up from 12% last October.

F) Analysts expect the fast-food industry to grow modestly this year. But the downturn is making companies rethink their strategies. Many are now introducing higher-priced items to entice(引诱) consumers away from $1specials. RFC, a division of Yum! Brands, which also owns Taco Bell and Pizza Hut, has launched a chicken sandwich that costs around $5. And in May Burger King introduced barbecue(烧烤) pork ribs at $7 for eight.

G) Companies are also trying to get customers to buy new and more items, including drinks. McDonald's started selling better coffee as a challenge to Starbucks. Its "McCafe" line now accounts for an estimated 6% of sales in America. Starbucks has sold rights to its Seattle's Best coffee brand to Burger King, which will start selling it later this year.

H) As fast-food companies shift from "super-size" to "more buys", they need to keep customer traffic high throughout the day. Many see breakfast as a big opportunity, and not just for fatty food. McDonald's will start selling porridge(粥) in America next year. Breakfast has the potential to be very profitable, says Sara Senatore of Bernstein, a research firm, because the margins can be high. Fast-food companies are also adding midday and late-night snacks, such as blended drinks and wraps. The idea is that by having a greater range of things on the menu, "we can sell to consumers products they want all day," says Rick Carucci, the chief financial officer of Yum! Brands.

I) But what about those growing waistlines? So far, fast-food firms have cleverly avoided government regulation. By providing healthy options, like salads and low-calorie sandwiches, they have at least given the impression of doing something about helping to fight obesity(肥胖症). These offerings are not necessarily loss-leaders, as they broaden the appeal of outlets to groups of diners that include some people who don't want to eat a burger. But customers cannot be forced to order salads instead of fries.

J) In the future, simply offering a healthy option may not be good enough. "Every packaged-food and restaurant company I know is concerned about regulation right now," says Mr. Palmer of UBS. America's health-reform bill, which Congress passed this year, requires restaurant chains with 20 or more outlets to put the calorie-content of items they serve on the menu. A study by the National Bureau of Economic Research, which tracked the effects on Starbucks of a similar calorie-posting law in New York City in 2007, found that the average calorie-count per transaction fell 6% and revenue increased 3% at Starbucks stores where a Dunkin Donuts outlet was nearby—a sign, it is said, that menu-labelling could favour chains that have more healthy offerings.

K) In order to avoid other legislation in America and elsewhere, fast-food companies will have to continue innovating(创新). Walt Riker of McDonald's claims the change it has made in its menu means it offers more healthy items than it did a few years ago. "We probably sell more vegetables, more milk, more salads, more apples than any restaurant business in the world," he says. But the recent proposal by a county in California to ban McDonald's from including toys in its high-calorie "Happy Meals", because legislators believe it attracts children to unhealthy food, suggests there is a lot more left to do.

questions.stem: A newly-passed law asks big fast-food chains to specify the calorie count of what they serve on the menu.
questions.passage:
The Changes Facing Fast Food

A) Fast-food firms have to be a thick-skinned bunch. Health experts regularly criticise them severely for selling food that makes people fat. Critics even complain that McDonald's, whose logo symbolises calorie excess, should not have been allowed to sponsor the World Cup. These are things fast-food firms have learnt to cope with. But not perhaps for much longer. The burger business faces more pressure from regulators at a time when it is already adapting strategies in response to shifts in the global economy.

B) Fast food was once thought to be recession-proof. When consumers need to cut spending, the logic goes, cheap meals like Big Macs and Whoppers become even more attractive. Such "trading down" proved true for much of the latest recession, when fast-food companies picked up customers who could no longer afford to eat at casual restaurants. Traffic was boosted in America, the home of fast food, with discounts and promotions, such as $1 menus and cheap combination meals.

C) As a result, fast-food chains have weathered the recession better than their more expensive competitors. In 2009 sales at full-service restaurants in America fell by more than 6%, but total sales remained about the same at fast-food chains. In some markets, such as Japan, France and Britain, total spending on fast food increased. Same-store sales in America at McDonald's, the world's largest fast-food company, did not decline throughout the downturn. Panera Bread, an American fast-food chain known for its fresh ingredients, performed well, too, because it offers higher-quality food at lower prices than restaurants.

D) But not all fast-food companies have been as fortunate. Many, such as Burger King, have seen sales fall. In a severe recession, while some people trade down to fast food, many others eat at home more frequently to save money. David Palmer, an analyst at UBS, a bank, says smaller fast-food chains in America, such as Jack in the Box and Carl's Jr., have been hit particularly hard in this downturn because they are competing with the global giant McDonald, which increased spending on advertising by more than 7% last year as others cut back.

E) Some fast-food companies also sacrificed their own profits by trying to give customers better value. During the recession companies set prices low, hoping that once they had tempted customers through the door they would be persuaded to order more expensive items. But in many cases that strategy did not work. Last year Burger franchisees(特许经营人) sued(起诉) the company over its double-cheeseburger promotion, claiming it was unfair for them to be required to sell these for $1 when they cost $1.10 to make. In May a judge ruled in favour of Burger King. Nevertheless, the company may still be cursing its decision to promote cheap choices over more expensive ones because items on its "value menu" now account for around 20% of all sales, up from 12% last October.

F) Analysts expect the fast-food industry to grow modestly this year. But the downturn is making companies rethink their strategies. Many are now introducing higher-priced items to entice(引诱) consumers away from $1specials. RFC, a division of Yum! Brands, which also owns Taco Bell and Pizza Hut, has launched a chicken sandwich that costs around $5. And in May Burger King introduced barbecue(烧烤) pork ribs at $7 for eight.

G) Companies are also trying to get customers to buy new and more items, including drinks. McDonald's started selling better coffee as a challenge to Starbucks. Its "McCafe" line now accounts for an estimated 6% of sales in America. Starbucks has sold rights to its Seattle's Best coffee brand to Burger King, which will start selling it later this year.

H) As fast-food companies shift from "super-size" to "more buys", they need to keep customer traffic high throughout the day. Many see breakfast as a big opportunity, and not just for fatty food. McDonald's will start selling porridge(粥) in America next year. Breakfast has the potential to be very profitable, says Sara Senatore of Bernstein, a research firm, because the margins can be high. Fast-food companies are also adding midday and late-night snacks, such as blended drinks and wraps. The idea is that by having a greater range of things on the menu, "we can sell to consumers products they want all day," says Rick Carucci, the chief financial officer of Yum! Brands.

I) But what about those growing waistlines? So far, fast-food firms have cleverly avoided government regulation. By providing healthy options, like salads and low-calorie sandwiches, they have at least given the impression of doing something about helping to fight obesity(肥胖症). These offerings are not necessarily loss-leaders, as they broaden the appeal of outlets to groups of diners that include some people who don't want to eat a burger. But customers cannot be forced to order salads instead of fries.

J) In the future, simply offering a healthy option may not be good enough. "Every packaged-food and restaurant company I know is concerned about regulation right now," says Mr. Palmer of UBS. America's health-reform bill, which Congress passed this year, requires restaurant chains with 20 or more outlets to put the calorie-content of items they serve on the menu. A study by the National Bureau of Economic Research, which tracked the effects on Starbucks of a similar calorie-posting law in New York City in 2007, found that the average calorie-count per transaction fell 6% and revenue increased 3% at Starbucks stores where a Dunkin Donuts outlet was nearby—a sign, it is said, that menu-labelling could favour chains that have more healthy offerings.

K) In order to avoid other legislation in America and elsewhere, fast-food companies will have to continue innovating(创新). Walt Riker of McDonald's claims the change it has made in its menu means it offers more healthy items than it did a few years ago. "We probably sell more vegetables, more milk, more salads, more apples than any restaurant business in the world," he says. But the recent proposal by a county in California to ban McDonald's from including toys in its high-calorie "Happy Meals", because legislators believe it attracts children to unhealthy food, suggests there is a lot more left to do.

questions.stem: What is people's common expectation of a high-factor sunscreen?
options: A) It will delay the occurrence of skin cancer.
B) It will protect them from sunburn.
C) It will keep their skin smooth and fair.
D) It will work for people of any skin color.
questions.passage:
If you think a high-factor sunscreen(防晒霜) keeps you safe from harmful rays, you may be wrong. Research in this week's Nature shows that while factor 50 reduces the number of melanomas(黑瘤) and delays their occurrence, it can't prevent them. Melanomas are the most aggressive skin cancers. You have a higher risk if you have red or blond hair, fair skin, blue or green eyes, or sunburn easily, or if a close relative has had one. Melanomas are more common if you have periodic intense exposure to the sun. Other skin cancers are increasingly likely with long-term exposure.

There is continuing debate as to how effective sunscreen is in reducing melanomas—the evidence is weaker than it is for preventing other types of skin cancer. A 2011 Australian study of 1,621 people found that people randomly selected to apply sunscreen daily had half the rate of melanomas of people who used cream as needed. A second study, comparing 1,167 people with melanomas to 1,101 who didn't have the cancer, found that using sunscreen routinely, alongside other protection such as hats, long sleeves or staying in the shade, did give some protection. This study said other forms of sun protection—not sunscreen—seemed most beneficial. The study relied on people remembering what they had done over each decade of their lives, so it's not entirely reliable. But it seems reasonable to think sunscreen gives people a false sense of security in the sun.

Many people also don't use sunscreen properly—applying insufficient amounts, failing to reapply after a couple of hours and staying in the sun too long. It is sunburn that is most worrying—recent research shows five episodes of sunburn in the teenage years increase the risk of all skin cancers.

The good news is that a combination of sunscreen and covering up can reduce melanoma rates, as shown by Australian figures from their slip-slop-slap campaign. So if there is a heat wave this summer, it would be best for us, too, to slip on a shirt, slop on(补上) sunscreen and slap on a hat.

writing.model:
The black-and-white cartoon presents a thought-provoking scene. On the left, a boy in a cap stares at his
smartphone and asks a tall, startled adult beside him, "Why am I going to school if my phone already knows
everything?" The child clearly believes that a device holding all the answers has made classrooms unnecessary.
This innocent question reveals a common misunderstanding: the boy equates going to school with merely
collecting facts. In his eyes, since a phone can instantly deliver any piece of information, education seems
pointless. Yet he confuses "having access to knowledge" with "truly possessing it." A phone can store data, but
it cannot teach a person how to reason, question, cooperate or judge right from wrong.
In fact, school shapes far more than our memory. It trains us to think independently, to communicate with
others and to grow into responsible adults—abilities no search engine can hand out. Therefore, we should tell
children like this boy that a smartphone is only a tool, while genuine learning still begins in the classroom.
